method.luminance: WCAG 2.x relative luminance with sRGB linearisation ((c+0.055)/1.055)^2.4, threshold 0.04045
method.alpha: semi-transparent colours are composited over their background (and toasts over the #fafafa page) before measuring
method.suggestions: nearest colour with the same hue and saturation (HSL lightness moved) that meets the requirement

notes: Bulma 0.9 picks the invert with its own luminance (squares instead of ^2.4) and a 0.55 threshold. The WCAG crossover where black and white text give equal contrast is a luminance of about 0.18, so colours between roughly 0.18 and 0.55 get white text although dark text would contrast better.

$grey-light, $grey-dark, $black and $white are overridden in main.scss, which also changes Bulma values derived from them ($background = $grey-light #c5c6c6 is the default tag/notification background; $text = $grey-dark #434242).

Navbar.vue, Sidebar.vue, AppMain.vue and FooterBar.vue import Bulma utilities without main.scss, so any colour variable used in their <style> blocks would be Bulma defaults. Today they only use mixins and hard-coded values.
